plan: Eight new SAT R&W items in the stricter hard-item design (every distractor partly supported): circumspect versus speculative (WIC), babbling explanation applied to father words, minimum-wage text with a qualification, steady-decline rainfall table with true-but-insufficient distractors, comma with but, past perfect progressive, admittedly concession, animal tool-use generalization. Difficulty provisional.

passages.title: A change in tone
passages.text: The chemist's early papers were notably ______, hedging nearly every conclusion and noting the limits of each experiment, but her later work stated its claims with striking confidence.

passages.title: Words for parents
passages.text: In many unrelated languages, the word for "mother" begins with an m sound. One explanation is that m is among the first sounds infants make, since it requires only closing the lips while using the voice, and parents may have taken an infant's early babbling as a name for the mother. If this explanation is correct, words for "father" in many unrelated languages would also be expected to ______

passages.title: Minimum wage studies
passages.text: Economists have often described raising the minimum wage as a tradeoff: workers who keep their jobs earn more, but fewer jobs are available. A growing number of studies, however, have found little or no loss of employment after moderate increases. These findings do not show that every increase is harmless. Most of the studies examined raises of modest size, and the effects of much larger increases remain uncertain.

passages.title: Rainfall in two regions
passages.text:
Average yearly rainfall, in millimeters, in two regions:
Region X: 820 in 2010; 760 in 2015; 700 in 2020.
Region Y: 640 in 2010; 650 in 2015; 600 in 2020.
A researcher claims that rainfall declined steadily in Region X over this period, whereas rainfall in Region Y did not decline consistently.

passages.title: A reopened archive
passages.text: The city's archive had been closed to the public for ______ researchers were finally admitted in 2019, after a team of librarians had finished cataloging its contents.

passages.title: A storm at the summit
passages.text: By the time the rescue team reached the summit, the storm ______ for nearly six hours, and two of the stranded climbers were showing signs of exhaustion.

passages.title: An abrupt ending
passages.text: Critics have called the novel's ending abrupt. ______ the final chapter is only two pages long and leaves several subplots unresolved. Yet the abruptness seems deliberate: the narrator, who has controlled every detail of the story, finally loses control of it.

passages.title: Animal tools
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Sea otters float on their backs and use rocks to crack open shellfish.
- New Caledonian crows shape twigs and leaves into hooks for pulling insects from holes.
- Some octopuses carry coconut shell halves and assemble them into shelters.
- Sea otters are mammals, crows are birds, and octopuses are mollusks.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: hedging nearly every conclusion and noting the limits of each experiment
candidates.explanation: Papers that hedge their conclusions and note their limits are cautious and careful, which is "circumspect," in contrast to the confident later work.

A.rationale: Speculative work advances guesses beyond the evidence, the opposite of hedging conclusions and noting limits.

C.rationale: Perfunctory work is careless or minimal, but hedging every conclusion and noting each limit shows care.

D.rationale: Nothing suggests the early papers copied others' work.

hints: What do "hedging" and "noting the limits" have in common?
candidates.remember: Use both the description and the contrast after "but" to define the blank.

candidates.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: begin with an m sound as often as words for "mother" do.
choices.B: differ from one another as much as most other words in those languages do.
choices.C: have been borrowed long ago from a single shared ancestral language.
choices.D: use sounds that infants are able to produce very early in life.

candidates.evidence: m is among the first sounds infants make
candidates.explanation: The explanation rests on infants' earliest sounds. If it is right, other parent words formed from babbling should also use sounds infants make early, not necessarily m.

A.rationale: The explanation predicts early sounds, not specifically m; giving both parents the same sound would not follow.

B.rationale: The explanation predicts similarity in early sounds, not ordinary variation.

C.rationale: Borrowing is an alternative explanation, not a prediction of the infant-babbling one.

hints: What feature of m does the explanation rely on?

strategy.explanation: Generalize the mechanism, not the specific sound.

candidates.remember: When applying an explanation, carry over its mechanism, not its specific example.

candidates.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To note that evidence has challenged a common view while warning against overextending it
choices.B: To argue that raising the minimum wage has never reduced the number of jobs available
choices.C: To explain why many economists have viewed minimum wage increases as a tradeoff
choices.D: To recommend a specific size for future increases in the minimum wage across the country

candidates.evidence: These findings do not show that every increase is harmless.
candidates.explanation: The text presents a common view, reports evidence against it, and then limits what that evidence shows; A captures both the challenge and the caution.

B.rationale: The text says the effects of larger increases are uncertain, so it does not claim no increase reduces jobs.

C.rationale: This describes only the first sentence; most of the text concerns new evidence and its limits.

D.rationale: The text recommends no particular increase.

hints: What does the text do after reporting the new studies?

strategy.explanation: Include the final caution in your summary.

candidates.remember: A purpose answer must cover a text's qualification, not just its main claim.

candidates.stem: Which choice best uses data from the table to support the researcher's claim?

choices.A: Region X received more rainfall than Region Y did in each of the three years shown in the table.
choices.B: Region Y received 600 millimeters of rainfall in 2020, which was 40 millimeters less than in 2010.
choices.C: Region X fell from 820 to 760 to 700 mm, while Region Y rose from 640 to 650 before falling to 600.
choices.D: Both regions received less rainfall in 2020 than in 2010, and Region X had the larger total decline.

candidates.evidence: whereas rainfall in Region Y did not decline consistently
candidates.explanation: A steady decline means falling at each step; only C shows Region X falling each time and Region Y rising before it fell.

A.rationale: This compares amounts, not whether each region's rainfall declined steadily.

B.rationale: This suggests Region Y declined and ignores its rise from 2010 to 2015, which the claim depends on.

D.rationale: Comparing only the endpoints hides whether either decline was steady.

hints: What does "steadily" require you to check?

strategy.explanation: Look at every year, not just the first and last.

candidates.remember: Claims about trends need every data point, not just the endpoints.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.explanation: Each side of the blank is an independent clause, and the second contrasts with the first, so a comma followed by "but" is correct.

A.rationale: Two independent clauses joined by "but" need a comma before the conjunction.

B.rationale: A comma alone cannot join two independent clauses; this is a comma splice.

C.rationale: A semicolon is not used before a coordinating conjunction joining two clauses.

strategy.explanation: Check how the two clauses are joined.

candidates.remember: Join two independent clauses with a comma plus a coordinating conjunction.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.evidence: By the time the rescue team reached the summit
candidates.explanation: The storm's raging continued up to a past moment, the team's arrival, so the past perfect progressive "had been raging" fits.

B.rationale: The present perfect does not fit an action completed before a past moment ("reached the summit").

C.rationale: The present tense does not fit the past-tense narrative.

D.rationale: The future perfect does not fit a past event.

hints: Is the storm's raging before or after the team arrived?

strategy.explanation: Use "By the time ... reached" to set the tense.

candidates.remember: Use "had been" + -ing for an action ongoing up to a past moment.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
candidates.explanation: The writer concedes facts that support the critics before arguing, with "Yet," that the abruptness is intentional, so the concession word "Admittedly" fits.

A.rationale: The second sentence does not replace the critics' view; it gives facts that support it.

B.rationale: The second sentence does not describe a different but similar case.

D.rationale: The chapter's length is not a result of the critics' description; it is evidence for it.

hints: Is the writer agreeing with the critics, and what happens in the next sentence?
candidates.remember: "Admittedly" grants a point that the writer will then answer.

candidates.stem: The student wants to make a generalization about tool use in animals. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: New Caledonian crows shape twigs and leaves into hooks that they use to pull insects out of holes.
choices.B: Animals as different as otters, crows, and octopuses all use objects as tools for food or shelter.
choices.C: Sea otters are mammals, crows are birds, and octopuses are mollusks, three very different groups.
choices.D: Some octopuses carry coconut shell halves and assemble them into shelters when they need protection.

candidates.evidence: Sea otters are mammals, crows are birds, and octopuses are mollusks.
candidates.explanation: Only B draws a general statement about tool use across very different kinds of animals, supported by examples from the notes.

A.rationale: This describes one species and does not generalize.

C.rationale: This states the groups but never mentions tool use.

D.rationale: This describes one species and does not generalize.

hints: Which choice makes a statement about animals in general?

strategy.explanation: Look for a claim that covers all the examples.

candidates.remember: A generalization states what several examples have in common.
